stem: A freight train leaves a station in Lahore and travels at a constant speed of 60 kilometers per hour. One hour later, an express train leaves the same station on a parallel track and travels in the same direction at a constant speed of 90 kilometers per hour. How many kilometers from the station will the express train be when it catches up with the freight train?
solution: Let \(t\) be the express train's travel time in hours. The freight train has then traveled \(t + 1\) hours.
They have gone the same distance \(d\): \(d = 60(t + 1)\) and \(d = 90t\).
verify:
t, d = symbols('t d')
sol = solve([d - 60*(t + 1), d - 90*t], [t, d])
assert sol == {t: 2, d: 180}
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [sol[d]]
